question_en: What are the specific name and manufacturer of the device shown in the figure?
answer: Stempelmaschine für streng verrechenbare Abdrücke; I. J. Bachrach & Harfner
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · P2-2-2-B01

## Step 01 · Formulate usage hypotheses from the lever, stamping head, and number box

**Action:** Observe the current physical photograph; one may attempt search combinations ranging from broad to narrow, such as `antique stamping press counter`, `Stempelmaschine Zählwerk`, or `Signettenpresse`.

**Evidence Observation:** The device has a long base and an open arched frame. A long lever extends from a handle on the left, crosses a central pivot, and reaches a disc on the upper right. Vertical guide rods are located at the front, and the top of the column features a horizontal box with positions for displaying numbers. Linkages and working mechanisms are also present at the bottom. This combination supports the hypothesis of a manual stamping/embossing device equipped with a counting mechanism, but the number box does not necessarily mean the machine prints consecutive numbers on paper. The manufacturer cannot be identified from the photograph alone.

**Result of this step:** Prioritize searching for stamping, postal, or fiscal stamping devices equipped with counters; the specific name must be determined by specific literature and the identical image.

## Step 02 · Obtain the name and manufacturer corresponding to the identical image from fiscal philately literature

**Action:** Read the entry `S wie Stempelmaschinen` on page 32 of Wolfgang Mintert's "Das A bis Z der Fiskalphilatelie," and jointly examine the main text, the physical photograph, and the technical diagram on the same page.

https://www.vindobona.club/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/2025-Mintert-Fiskalphilatelie.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The physical photograph in the lower left of the page shares the same wallpaper background, number box, upper-right disc, lever, and base structure as the input image, making it the direct source of the figure in question. The main text attributes the instrument to the Vienna firm `I. J. Bachrach & Harfner`, provides the patent application name `Stempelmaschine für streng verrechenbare Abdrücke`, and explains that the stamping machine is connected to a counting device, suitable for impressions requiring strict accounting. 1893 is the patent application year mentioned in this entry, not a manufacturing year or model suffix determined from the photograph.

**Result of this step:** The specific name and manufacturer have been linked by the entry containing the identical image; "counter-equipped fiscal stamping machine / Signettenpresse" can serve as a functional explanation.

## Step 03 · Verify the technical diagram and function in another article

**Action:** Read the article by Arnold Goller on page 35 of "Vindobona Vereinsnachrichten" 3/2025, and compare Figure 2 with the relevant descriptions.

https://vindobona.club/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Vindobona-Nachrichten-3-2025.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The article refers to the illustrated device as a `Signettenpresse` by Bachrach & Harfner, notes that it has a built-in counting mechanism, and discusses the context of newspaper fiscal stamps and fee collection. The elevated number box, vertical column, counterweight disc on the upper right, long lever, arched frame, and base linkages on the reprinted technical diagram correspond simultaneously with the photograph. The diagram and the photograph have different perspectives; the left end of the lever in the diagram extends beyond the drawing edge, so one should not fabricate another model simply because the handle curve is not fully displayed. Although the two authors are different, the technical diagrams used may share the same source; currently, only secondary reprints are available, so one cannot claim to have obtained two independent original patents.

**Result of this step:** The structure and fiscal stamping usage align with the entry containing the identical image, and the name has cross-referenced textual support; do not accumulate two diagram reprints into evidence of independent patents.

## Step 04 · Compare with similar stamping and postal devices

**Action:** Use the original patent diagram of the Pomeroy Seal-press, the archived old webpage of the Pearson Hill parallel motion canceling machine from the museum, and the diagram of the Latham "Monitor" embosser to check for other plausible explanations.

https://patents.google.com/patent/US914672A/en

https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/0a/e5/c1/bee1c2fb41f418/US914672.pdf

https://www.postoffice.alectritton.co.uk/page/cancelling-parallel/

https://www.postoffice.alectritton.co.uk/uploads/2002_0941i_0.jpg

https://bookbindersmuseum.org/collections/equipment/stamper-latham-american-1916/

**Evidence Observation:** Pomeroy's desktop C-shaped stamping press has a short head and a top handle, lacking the target's tall column number box and the long rod with a disc counterweight spanning the body; the `counter die` in the patent refers to the lower die and should not be mistranslated as a numerical counter. Photographs of the Pearson Hill show a short straight pressing rod at the front and a low long base, lacking the target's elevated horizontal box and wide arched frame. The Latham diagram shows a nearly closed rounded rectangular frame, a wide pressing plate, and a top adjustment screw, with the long handle located on the right side of the body, also lacking the target combination. These are usage/structural neighbors with diagrams, not a claim that all variants from the same manufacturer have been found.

**Result of this step:** The neighbor comparison is consistent with the overall technical diagram of the target; the name and manufacturer from the original entry with the identical image remain the most sufficient.

## Step 05 · Limit the answer to information supported by literature

**Action:** Output the formal name and manufacturer from the literature, and verify whether the year or collection location has been misused.

**Evidence Observation:** Mintert explicitly states that the physical photograph comes from an old collection lacking further provenance; another text mentions a museum description, which is also insufficient to confirm the current collection location of this single item in the photograph. The 1910 postal canceling machine described elsewhere on the same page cannot be transplanted as the identity of the target. The device name and manufacturer required by the question have been closed; there is no need to add unconfirmed collection numbers or a "1893 model."

**Result of this step:** Stop searching.

**Formal Answer:**

Stempelmaschine für streng verrechenbare Abdrücke；I. J. Bachrach & Harfner
